name: Thresholds

subjectOf.text: The quantitative measures used in systemic risk assessment are not codified in statute, so the FSOC can alter its thresholds and its analysis through rulemaking.
subjectOf.abstract: the quantitative systemic risk assessment measures are not specifically codified and the FSOC can change thresholds and analysis via the rule making process
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Systemic Risk of Private Funds after the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2470008

subjectOf.text: Commonly managed investment funds holding $50 billion or more in aggregate total consolidated assets can be designated systemically important, and following a similar investment strategy across those funds makes designation more likely.
subjectOf.abstract: Commonly managed investment funds that manage $50 billion or more in the aggregate of total consolidated assets could be designated a SIFI, particularly if such funds all follow a similar investment strategy.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Systemic Risk of Private Funds after the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2470008
scope_conditions: aggregate total consolidated assets at or above $50 billion
funds under common management pursuing similar strategies

subjectOf.text: Form PF information addresses most of the FSOC's stage one thresholds either directly or indirectly, so the mechanical screen runs largely on adviser reported data.

subjectOf.text: A candidate is accepted when its weighted valid share exceeds the threshold of one half, and a candidate within a tenth of that threshold is contested, receives four more validators, and is bound by the recomputed share.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: Five validators are seated per candidate from a roster of twenty, and each votes independently.
The rule replaces the parent protocol's two rounds with a single assessment and a threshold-triggered second look.

subjectOf.text: A threshold arm that accepts too few candidates fills the shortfall uniformly from rejected candidates, and an arm whose minimum over generations of the seed-mean fill-free share falls below 0.98 in a family has its tests there invalidated.

Validator compute is not equal across arms, so an equal candidate budget does not mean equal assessment cost.

subjectOf.text: The frozen pass rule requires, on the five-run means from generation 0 to 9, a full-replacement perplexity rise of at least 4.0 with a margin of at least 2.0 over the rise under ten percent retention, with the thresholds sitting at fractions of the reported change so the rule does not depend on which published baseline was meant, and a miss blocks reading anything else.
